title: Halley Financial - hosting path & migration discovery
summary: Intro discovery to map Halley Financial's current OpenAI-based deployment, evaluate tradeoffs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem), identify blockers (SOC2, encryption/KMS, low-latency inference), and agree next steps for a pilot and benchmark run using sample prompts and their eval suite.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + security pack
SE to run compatibility checklist with Halley's eval corpus
Schedule 1-week pilot: dedicated capacity spike (dates TBD)
Send pricing for hosted vs dedicated reserved 6-month commit
action_items: Ravi: run quick vLLM/TGI model load with Halley eval set and share perf matrix (due 2027-08-10)
Maya: send SOC2 + SSO/KMS integration docs and pricing sheet (due 2027-08-05)
Samir: provide 2 canonical prompt sets and a 1GB sample dataset for KV cache trials (due 2027-08-06)
Leah: confirm procurement timeline and legal requirements for Private deployment (due 2027-08-12)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick off, can folks introduce themselves?
[00:06] Samir Khan: sure, samir here, head of ml at halley financial, we've been on openai for our prod generation and embeddings for about 18 months.
[00:13] Leah Ortiz: leah, cto. main thing for us is security and latency for downstream trading alerts, so that's the bar.
[00:20] Tim Wu: tim, infrastructure. i run the k8s clusters and our on-prem hardware for sensitive workloads.
[00:25] Maya Chen: awesome — quick agenda: map current architecture, goals (latency/cost/sla), migration blockers, and pilot next steps. ravi from our solutions engineering group will do the deep dive.
[00:34] Ravi Patel: hi all, quick question — are you calling OpenAI via API for both chat completions and embeddings?
[00:39] Samir Khan: yes, embeddings for index search, chat for assistant workflows. costs spiked after q1, and we need consistent p99 latency under 200ms for short prompts.
[00:47] Ravi Patel: got it. when you say p99 200ms is that token-latency or end-to-end including network?
[00:52] Samir Khan: our SLA target is end-to-end from request to first token. realistically most of the time it's 150-300ms today depending on model.
[01:00] Ravi Patel: ok, a couple things to consider: hosted vs dedicated vs private. hosted gives fastest onboarding and managed models. dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. private (VPC/on-prem) addresses compliance but adds ops overhead.
[01:14] Leah Ortiz: for our regulated clients, on-prem or VPC is needed for some data classes; SOC2 and KMS integration non-negotiable. can you do customer-managed KMS and audit logs?
[01:23] Maya Chen: yes, our Private offering supports customer KMS/HSM and audit logs; we also provide a private control plane. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:31] Tim Wu: how about model parity — we run a vllm-based stack for cost reasons in staging and TGI in some endpoints. concerns about tokenization differences and quantization drift when moving between runtimes.
[01:41] Ravi Patel: totally — we've done a few migrations from vLLM/TGI setups. main compatibility issues are: tokenizer versions (bpe vs byte-level), kv cache format differences, and quantized weight layout. for many open models it's straightforward but there are edge cases.
[01:56] Samir Khan: have you seen hallucination differences after porting? our quality bar is strict — a single percentage point regression on our reranker is a big hit.
[02:03] Ravi Patel: yes, which is why we recommend eval parity runs. we can run your test suite on the same model variants in our hosted fleet and on dedicated capacity. we keep model variant metadata and seed settings to reduce nondeterminism.
[02:15] Leah Ortiz: what about throughput — can dedicated be autoscaled? our traffic pattern has big spikes during market opens.
[02:21] Maya Chen: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. we can set policy to maintain p95/p99 targets, and we expose token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console.
[02:32] Tim Wu: ok, two technical asks: 1) can we run a KV cache warmup test with a 1GB prefix set, 2) can we get a latency trace with distributed spans?
[02:42] Ravi Patel: yes to both. we can instrument tracing hooks; for KV cache we support prefix caching and will try to match your warmup pattern. we'll need the sample prefix corpus.
[02:51] Samir Khan: also, we use SAML SSO; any gotchas there?
[02:55] Maya Chen: we support SSO/SAML and RBAC; the security pack includes our SAML integration guide.
[03:01] Dana Reed: pricing — how does reserved capacity pricing compare to hosted? we want to know cost per 1M tokens.
[03:06] Maya Chen: i'll send a pricing sheet but generally hosted is usage-based and great for experimentation. dedicated reserved capacity with 6–12 month commits lowers unit cost significantly and gives latency predictability.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: to add — we also provide Optimize recommendations: batching and quantization profiles per workload to lower unit cost while keeping quality. quantization can affect outputs, so we'll test on your eval set.
[03:29] Samir Khan: curious about Azure OpenAI — we have some endpoints there. any migration lessons?
[03:33] Ravi Patel: Azure is similar to OpenAI in API shape but watch out for region egress and some model name mismatches. for all exits we map model equivalence and do eval parity testing.
[03:43] Leah Ortiz: legal: for Private we need a contract that allows on-prem install and outlines breach notification timelines. procurement is a 6–8 week process.
[03:50] Maya Chen: noted — we'll involve enterprise legal and share a template.
[03:54] Tim Wu: on the technical side, we want to keep inference close to market data with sub-200ms; can Redwood route requests by region and fall back to cheaper models if capacity constrained?
[04:03] Maya Chen: yes, smart routing policies are supported — latency-first routing with automatic fallback to compatible variants. we also allow routing by customer tier and region.
[04:12] Ravi Patel: quick clarification — when you say "cheaper models" do you mean smaller variants with quantization?
[04:15] Tim Wu: yes.
[04:18] Samir Khan: what's the process for a pilot? e.g., a week-long dedicated spike?
[04:22] Maya Chen: typical pilot: 1) we exchange security docs and contract terms, 2) SE runs compatibility and perf runs using your eval prompts and sample data, 3) we run a 7–14 day dedicated capacity spike with monitoring and handoff.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: i'll run an initial model-load test against your eval set and share raw latencies plus token-cost estimates.
[04:42] Dana Reed: any gotchas with TGI specifically? we run a mix of TGI servers and vLLM in staging.
[04:47] Ravi Patel: TGI often has custom optimizations; the key is to validate kernel paths and attention optimizations. Redwood's runtime picks kernels based on architecture and sequence length distribution, but we'll run parity checks.
[04:58] Samir Khan: can you preserve prompt context across long chats — KV cache compatibility again?
[05:03] Ravi Patel: yes, we've implemented continuous KV caching and prefix caching that matches common vLLM/TGI usage patterns; we'll test with your 1GB prefix.
[05:12] Leah Ortiz: circling back to security: do you support bringing our own HSM for key signing?
[05:16] Maya Chen: yes, private customers can integrate their HSM/KMS; we also provide audit logs and compliance telemetry.
[05:23] Tim Wu: for the benchmark, what metrics should we expect? latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, token cost, and quality regressions on reranker?
[05:31] Ravi Patel: exactly. and we'll include a diff of outputs for a subset of deterministic prompts so you can see any drift.
[05:39] Samir Khan: how long until we get a first pass?
[05:42] Maya Chen: action items are on us to deliver SOC2 and pricing by aug 5, and SE to run initial compatibility by aug 10. then we reconvene to schedule the dedicated spike.
[05:51] Leah Ortiz: sounds good. one more: can you support data residency in eu-west-1 for certain clients?
[05:56] Maya Chen: yes, we have regional hosting and can pin model serving to specific regions.
[06:01] Dana Reed: thanks everyone.
[06:03] Maya Chen: thanks — we'll follow up with the security pack and a proposed pilot dates.
[06:07] [call ends]
